title: Supply-chain Decision Ledger v1
description:
Append-only JSONL ledger recording Layer 3 supply-chain review decisions (spec §16.4, v2.6 — E-SC-7). Five entry kinds: `accept` (operator accepts a flagged dep as not-currently-actionable), `reject` (operator rejects the dep; remediation required), `pin-to-last-good` (operator pins to a known-good version pending upstream fix), `review-pending` (a review ticket has been opened but no human decision yet), `review-triaged` (a previously-pending review has been resolved; supersedes the pending entry).

Each line in the JSONL file is one entry. Readers reconstruct decision state by folding the stream chronologically; `review-triaged` entries supersede their `review-pending` predecessors via the `supersedes_ts` reference. Writes happen via the implementation's review CLI; the writer enforces schema compliance + operator-identity discipline. Never edit entries in place — corrections are new entries superseding old ones (append-only discipline; same shape as `domain-promotion-ledger-v1.schema.json`).

Language discipline: findings published outside the Brain (e.g., shared via §16.6 A2A signal) MUST use non-attributive language per §16.4. The `human_notes` and `agent_findings` fields are operator-internal; non-attributive language is RECOMMENDED but not required for internal-only fields. The `legal_disclaimer` field on the A2A envelope is the forcing function for external sharing.

name.description: Package name as it appears in its registry (e.g., 'litellm', 'serde', '@scope/pkg').

ecosystem.description: Ecosystem identifier. Conventional values match OSV.dev's ecosystem strings ('crates.io', 'PyPI', 'npm', 'Go', 'Maven', 'RubyGems', 'NuGet', etc.). Implementations MAY use additional values for ecosystems not yet covered by OSV.dev.

version_range.description: Optional version range affected (e.g., '>=1.82.7,<1.82.9' or 'all'). Implementation-defined format; semver-style ranges RECOMMENDED.

layer.description: Which §16 layer surfaced this signal. 1 = mechanical SCA (advisory match). 2 = vigilance (deep-signal heuristic). 3 = agent-assisted review (LLM-judge finding).

signal_kind.description: Implementation-defined identifier for the specific signal (e.g., 'osv-advisory:RUSTSEC-2024-0436', 'vigilance:publish-cadence-spike', 'agent:exfil-indicator').

advisory_id.description: If applicable, the canonical advisory identifier (CVE-YYYY-NNNNN, RUSTSEC-YYYY-NNNN, GHSA-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx, etc.).

source_uri.description: Optional pointer to the original signal source (advisory page, CMDB finding, agent-review report).

confidence.description: Confidence in [0, 1]. Layer 1 signals SHOULD report 1.0 (exact-match advisory). Layer 2/3 signals are probabilistic.

finding_kind.description: Machine-tag classification of the agent's finding (e.g., 'static:base64-payload', 'static:eval-introduced', 'static:network-endpoint-added', 'meta:maintainer-rotation', 'recommendation:pin-to-last-good').

summary.description: Short prose summary of the finding (one sentence). Non-attributive language RECOMMENDED.

evidence_uri.description: Optional pointer to the evidence (file path, URL to a diff, etc.).

confidence.description: Agent's self-reported confidence in [0, 1]. Operators SHOULD treat <0.7 as inconclusive.

from_version.description: The currently-installed (or proposed) version that triggered the review.

to_version.description: The version the operator decision targets (for accept/pin-to-last-good entries).

triggering_signals.description: All Layer 1 + Layer 2 + Layer 3 signals that motivated this decision. Empty array indicates a manual operator entry without sensor signals.

agent_findings.description: Layer 3 agent's findings, if a review was performed. Empty for accept/reject decisions made without agent involvement.

human_operator.description: Operator handle. Self-asserted in v1 (e.g., from environment variable). Implementations MAY use cryptographic identity in future versions.

human_notes.description: Free-text rationale from the operator. Forces the decision to be auditable in 18 months when the operator who made it has rotated off the project.

audit_reports.description: Optional paths to supporting audit reports (CMDB snapshot, agent-review report, calibration evidence, etc.).

human_notes.description: REQUIRED for `accept`. Documents WHY the dep was accepted as not-currently-actionable. Hygiene lever: silent acceptance is the failure mode this entry kind exists to prevent.

expires_at.description: Optional ISO-8601 date. After this date, the acceptance is considered stale and the operator MUST re-review. Implementations SHOULD surface stale acceptances in their CMDB output.

human_notes.description: REQUIRED for `reject`. Documents the rejection rationale and the remediation path (e.g., 'replace with X', 'fork and inline-vendor pending upstream fix', 'remove dep entirely').

from_version.description: REQUIRED for `pin-to-last-good`. The currently-installed (compromised or suspect) version.

to_version.description: REQUIRED for `pin-to-last-good`. The known-good version the dep is being pinned to.

human_notes.description: REQUIRED for `pin-to-last-good`. Documents the rationale (e.g., 'upstream fix pending; pin to last known-good 1.82.6 until 1.82.10 or later ships and is reviewed').

expires_at.description: Optional ISO-8601 date. After this date, the pin is considered stale and the operator MUST re-review (e.g., to confirm the upstream fix has shipped).

triggering_signals.description: REQUIRED, non-empty for `review-pending`. The signals that motivated opening the review ticket.

agent_findings.description: Optional agent findings produced when the ticket was opened.

human_operator.description: REQUIRED. Operator who opened the ticket. For system-opened tickets (e.g., the Layer 2 vigilance auto-create bridge), implementations MUST use the conventional value `'auto'` so the audit trail distinguishes system-opened from human-opened tickets. Per the 2026-04-26 PRE-RELEASE B10 fix: previously this field was optional with semantics 'MAY be the system itself for auto-opened tickets'; tightened to required because operator-identity discipline applies to every ledger entry kind (spec §16.4).

human_notes.description: Optional initial notes from the operator opening the ticket.

review_ticket_id.description: Implementation-defined ticket identifier (e.g., a path under `.claude/brain/supply-chain-tickets/`).

supersedes_ts.description: REQUIRED. The `ts` of the `review-pending` entry being resolved. Append-only supersede pattern (same as `domain-promotion-ledger-v1.schema.json`'s rollback).

resolution.description: REQUIRED. The decision the operator reached. `no-action` indicates the operator reviewed and decided no action was warranted (e.g., signal turned out to be a false positive).

human_notes.description: REQUIRED for `review-triaged`. Documents the resolution rationale; this is the auditable record of why the review reached its conclusion.

review_ticket_id.description: If the original `review-pending` carried a ticket id, the same id SHOULD be repeated here for cross-reference.
